newsitem.title: HONG KONG: WEEK AHEAD - HK stocks brace for volatile trade.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD - HK stocks brace for volatile trade.

text.p: A rapid ascent in Hong Kong share prices over recent weeks has left the market vulnerable to some volatility early this week as investors await the outcome of the U.S. Federal Reserve meeting on Tuesday, brokers said.
Although rotation into some lagging blue chips could drive the Hang Seng Index to new highs later in the week, the market as a whole was more vulnerable to the downside, they added.
"I would anticipate the early part of the week to be very volatile," said Miles Remington, sales trader at SocGen-Crosby Securities.
"There could be some possibility of a (U.S.) interest rate hike on Tuesday," he said.
Optimism on Wall Street helped drive the Hang Seng Index to all-time highs last week, with the blue chip index hitting an intra-day record high of 14,167.01 points on Thursday.
Over the week the Hang Seng Index gained 131.57 points, or 0.94 percent, to close at 14,062.37 but lost some momentum near the end of the week.

"There is a wait-and-see attitude," said Geoff Galbraith, institutional sales trader at NAVA SC Securities. He said investors would reassess their positions after Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting.

Renewed fears that the Fed would raise short term interest rates sent U.S. stocks sharply lower Friday. The rate jitters began to boil after news that U.S. housing starts rose by a stronger-than-expected 2.6 percent in April.

"If the Fed raises rates it will have a negative impact on the market in the sense that the market has really recently benefited fom the U.S. rally," said Frederick Tsang, head of research at BNP PrimeEast Securities.
"Also the U.S market is trading at record highs so the negative news would put some pressure on the market," he said.
But Tsang said if rates remained unchanged, the market could resume its uptrend with the interest-rate sensitive property sector, which has lagged the Hang Seng Index, a likely winner.
He expected the index to trade in a range of 13,800 to 14,300 points this week.

Remington said since the index had ended the week above 14,000, investors may chose that level as a platform. The index closed for the first time above that level on Wednesday, when it settled at a record close of 14,153.58.
But Remington said the downside in the week ahead could possibly be 13,600 points with the upside at 14,200.
Shares in global emerging markets investment house Regent Pacific Group Ltd are due to begin trading on Monday.

The company offered 170.5 million shares at HK$2.62 per share. The Hong Kong initial public offering of 42.63 million shares was 12.1 times subscribed and the 127.88 million shares offered to international investors was well over-subscribed, the company said.
Analysts expected a firm trading debut but said a lack of retail interest in the stock could limit the upside.
Chu Kong Shipping Development Co Ltd is also due to make its market debut next week. The shipping company offered 187.5 million shares at HK$1.20 each and the stock is due to begin trading on Friday.
